claim: The Polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2) plays a critical role in the control of growth, development, and adaptation to environmental fluctuations of most multicellular eukaryotes.
source: The catalytic activity of PRC2 is counteracted by Jumonji-type (JMJ) histone demethylases, which shapes the genomic distribution of H3K27me3.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about PRC2 function.

claim: The catalytic activity of PRC2 is counteracted by Jumonji-type (JMJ) histone demethylases.
source: The catalytic activity of PRC2 is counteracted by Jumonji-type (JMJ) histone demethylases, which shapes the genomic distribution of H3K27me3.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge.

claim: Jumonji-type histone demethylases shape the genomic distribution of H3K27me3.
source: The catalytic activity of PRC2 is counteracted by Jumonji-type (JMJ) histone demethylases, which shapes the genomic distribution of H3K27me3.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge.

claim: Two JMJ histone demethylases in Arabidopsis, EARLY FLOWERING 6 (ELF6) and RELATIVE OF EARLY FLOWERING 6 (REF6), play distinct roles in H3K27me3 and H3K27me1 homeostasis.
source: Here, we show that two JMJ histone demethylases in Arabidopsis, EARLY FLOWERING 6 (ELF6) and RELATIVE OF EARLY FLOWERING 6 (REF6), play distinct roles in H3K27me3 and H3K27me1 homeostasis.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by ChIP-seq data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Failure to reset H3K27me3 and H3K27me1 chromatin marks during sexual reproduction results in the transgenerational inheritance of histone marks.
source: We show that failure to reset these chromatin marks during sexual reproduction results in the transgenerational inheritance of histone marks, which cause a loss of DNA methylation at heterochromatic loci and transposon activation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by ChIP-seq data from epiER lines.

claim: Transgenerational inheritance of histone marks causes a loss of DNA methylation at heterochromatic loci.
source: We show that failure to reset these chromatin marks during sexual reproduction results in the transgenerational inheritance of histone marks, which cause a loss of DNA methylation at heterochromatic loci and transposon activation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by BS-seq data from epiER lines.

claim: Transgenerational inheritance of histone marks causes transposon activation.
source: We show that failure to reset these chromatin marks during sexual reproduction results in the transgenerational inheritance of histone marks, which cause a loss of DNA methylation at heterochromatic loci and transposon activation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by RNA-seq and transposon copy number data.

claim: Jumonji-type histone demethylases play a dual role in plants by helping to maintain transcriptional states through development and safeguard genome integrity during sexual reproduction.
source: Thus, Jumonji-type histone demethylases play a dual role in plants by helping to maintain transcriptional states through development and safeguard genome integrity during sexual reproduction.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, inferred from the combined data on transcriptional regulation and epigenetic inheritance.

claim: H3K9me2 and H3K27me1 have been associated with the repression of transposable elements (TEs) in constitutive heterochromatin.
source: Among these, the methylation of lysine 9 of histone H3 (H3K9me2) and H3K27me1 have been associated with the repression of transposable elements (TEs) in constitutive heterochromatin (Lindroth et al., 2004; Lippman et al., 2004; Mathieu et al., 2005)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: H3K27me3 has been associated with the repression of genes in euchromatic genome regions.
source: whereas other types of methylation, including H3K27me3, have been associated with the repression of genes in euchromatic genome regions (Berger, 2007; Pfluger and Wagner, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: H3K27me3 methylation is deposited by PRC2 and plays a crucial role in the development of most multicellular eukaryotes.
source: H3K27me3 methylation is deposited by PRC2 and plays a crucial role in the development of most multicellular eukaryotes (Laugesen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: In plants, H3K27me3 modification is found in approximately one quarter of protein-coding genes and is dynamically regulated during growth and development.
source: In plants, this modification is found in approximately one quarter of protein-coding genes and is dynamically regulated during growth and development (Lafos et al., 2011; Roudier et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: JMJ demethylases catalyze the specific removal of H3K27me3.
source: The activity of PRCs is counterbalanced by JMJ demethylases, which catalyze the specific removal of H3K27me3 (Liu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: In Arabidopsis, five histone demethylases (REF6, ELF6, JMJ13, JMJ30, and JMJ32) have been implicated in the demethylation of H3K27.
source: In Arabidopsis, five histone demethylases [RELATIVE OF EARLY FLOWERING 6 (REF6); EARLY FLOWERING 6 (ELF6); JUMONJI 13 (JMJ13); JUMONJI 30 (JMJ30); and JUMONJI 32 (JMJ32)] have been implicated in the demethylation of H3K27 (Crevillén et al., 2014; Gan et al., 2014; Lu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Inactivation of REF6 results in the ectopic accumulation of H3K27me3 at hundreds of loci, many of them involved in developmental patterning and environmental responses.
source: Inactivation of REF6 results in the ectopic accumulation of H3K27me3 at hundreds of loci, many of them involved in developmental patterning and environmental responses (Lu et al., 2011; Yan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: REF6 is recruited to a specific sequence motif through its zinc-finger domain.
source: It has been proposed that REF6 is recruited to a specific sequence motif through its zinc-finger domain (Cui et al., 2016; Lu et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: REF6 is also recruited by specific interactions with transcription factors.
source: however, others have shown that it is also recruited by specific interactions with transcription factors (Yan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The affinity of REF6 to chromatin is hindered by DNA methylation, which could explain why its activity is primarily found at euchromatic loci.
source: Moreover, it has been shown that the affinity of REF6 to chromatin is hindered by DNA methylation, which could explain why its activity is primarily found at euchromatic loci (Qiu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: REF6 acts redundantly with ELF6 and JMJ13 to restrict the accumulation of H3K27me3 in gene regulatory regions, thereby unlocking tissue-specific expression.
source: Previous studies have suggested that REF6 acts redundantly with ELF6 and JMJ13 to restrict the accumulation of H3K27me3 in gene regulatory regions, thereby unlocking tissue-specific expression (Yan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: REF6, ELF6, JMJ30 and JMJ32 specifically remove methyl groups from H3K27me3 and H3K27me2 but not from H3K27me1.
source: Importantly, REF6, ELF6, JMJ30 and JMJ32 appear to specifically remove methyl groups from H3K27me3 and H3K27me2 but not from H3K27me1 (Crevillén et al., 2014; Gan et al., 2014; Lu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: H3K27me1 in Arabidopsis is associated with constitutive heterochromatin, where it is deposited by ARABIDOPSIS TRITHORAX-RELATED PROTEIN5 (ATXR5) and ATRX6.
source: Previous investigations have shown that H3K27me1 in Arabidopsis is associated with constitutive heterochromatin, where it is deposited by ARABIDOPSIS TRITHORAX-RELATED PROTEIN5 (ATXR5) and ATRX6 (Jacob et al., 2009; Jacob et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: H3K27me1 is also found in euchromatin in mammals and plants.
source: However, several studies in mammals and plants have shown that H3K27me1 is also found in euchromatin (Fuchs et al., 2008; Jacob et al., 2009; Vakoc et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: H3K27me3 in euchromatin is thought to be actively re-set during sexual reproduction.
source: The presence of H3K27me3 in euchromatin is thought to be actively re-set during sexual reproduction – a view supported by studies in Arabidopsis showing that ELF6, REF6 and JMJ13 are necessary to reset and prevent the inheritance of this epigenetic mark to the offspring (Crevillén et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2019; Zheng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: ELF6, REF6 and JMJ13 are necessary to reset and prevent the inheritance of H3K27me3 to the offspring.
source: The presence of H3K27me3 in euchromatin is thought to be actively re-set during sexual reproduction – a view supported by studies in Arabidopsis showing that ELF6, REF6 and JMJ13 are necessary to reset and prevent the inheritance of this epigenetic mark to the offspring (Crevillén et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2019; Zheng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: elf6-C plants displayed an early flowering phenotype characterized by a reduced number of rosette leaves at bolting.
source: Similar to previous reports, we found that our elf6-C plants displayed an early flowering phenotype characterized by a reduced number of rosette leaves at bolting (Jeong et al., 2009; Noh et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a phenotypic observation from the study, consistent with previous reports.

claim: ref6-5 plants displayed a late flowering phenotype and an increased number of rosette leaves at bolting stage.
source: Conversely, ref6-5 plants displayed a late flowering phenotype and an increased number of rosette leaves at bolting stage (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: This is a phenotypic observation from the study, supported by figure data.

claim: elf6-C/ref6-5 double mutant plants displayed pleiotropic growth phenotypes, including increased number of petals and pleiotropic defects in leaf morphology, such as serrations and downward curling.
source: By manual crossing, we generated elf6-C/ref6-5 double mutant plants, which displayed pleiotropic growth phenotypes, including increased number of petals and pleiotropic defects in leaf morphology, such as serrations and downward curling (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 2C–D).
evidence: This is a phenotypic observation from the study, supported by figure data.

claim: Double mutant plants displayed a reduction in silique length.
source: In all combinations tested, double mutant plants displayed a reduction in silique length (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2E), thus suggesting that these mutations redundantly affect plant fertility.
evidence: This is a phenotypic observation from the study, supported by figure data.

claim: Seeds from ref6-5 and elf6-C/ref6-5 contained embryos with patterning defects.
source: Microscopy analysis of developing seeds revealed that while embryo development in elf6-C was normal, seeds from ref6-5 and elf6-C/ref6-5 contained embryos with patterning defects (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an observation from microscopy analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: Embryonic abnormalities in ref6-5 and elf6-C/ref6-5 did not affect seed germination rates.
source: However, these embryonic abnormalities did not affect seed germination rates (Figure 1—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This is an observation from germination assays, supported by figure data.

claim: The accumulation of H3K27me3 within genes was more pronounced in ref6-5 than in elf6-C.
source: Overall, the accumulation of H3K27me3 within genes was more pronounced in ref6-5 than in elf6-C (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from ChIP-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: Most of the hyper-methylated genes found in elf6 (75%) were hyper-methylated to a greater extent in both ref6-5 and elf6-C/ref6-5.
source: Most of the hyper-methylated genes found in elf6 (75%) were hyper-methylated to a greater extent in both ref6-5 and elf6-C/ref6-5, suggesting that these histone demethylases have partially overlapping yet distinct roles in the control of H3K27me3 homeostasis in Arabidopsis (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplements 3–4).
evidence: This is a finding from ChIP-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: There is a strong correlation between genes that were both hyper-methylated at H3K27me3 and down-regulated.
source: When combining transcriptomic and H3K27me3 ChIP-seq data, we found a strong correlation primarily between genes that were both hyper-methylated at H3K27me3 and down-regulated, thus indicating that this epigenetic mark contributes to their transcriptional repression (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplements 5–6).
evidence: This is a finding from combined RNA-seq and ChIP-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: Most of the genes targeted by REF6 accumulate high levels of H3K27me1 in wild-type.
source: To test this hypothesis, we determined the distribution of H3K27me1 through ChIP-seq assays and found that most of the genes targeted by REF6 accumulate high levels of H3K27me1 in wild-type (Figure 2A–C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from ChIP-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: Large-scale H3K27me1 accumulation in atxr5/atxr6 mutants was significantly reduced at pericentromeric heterochromatin.
source: As previously described, large-scale H3K27me1 accumulation in these mutants was significantly reduced at pericentromeric heterochromatin (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from ChIP-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: In atxr5/atxr6 lines the levels of H3K27me1 increased in gene-rich regions.
source: However, we noticed that in atxr5/atxr6 lines the levels of this histone mark increased in gene-rich regions, pointing to the existence of an alternative pathway for H3K27me1 deposition in euchromatin.
evidence: This is a finding from ChIP-seq analysis, leading to an inference about an alternative pathway.

claim: The loss of REF6 activity results in both the accumulation of H3K27me3 and a drastic reduction in H3K27me1 at genes targeted by REF6.
source: We found that the loss of REF6 activity results in both the accumulation of H3K27me3 and a drastic reduction in H3K27me1 at those loci, while the loss of ELF6 did not have an effect (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from ChIP-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: The loss of ELF6 did not affect H3K27me1 levels at genes targeted by REF6.
source: We found that the loss of REF6 activity results in both the accumulation of H3K27me3 and a drastic reduction in H3K27me1 at those loci, while the loss of ELF6 did not have an effect (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from ChIP-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: The accumulation of H3K27me3 in ref6-5 was associated with a complete loss of H3K27me1 at genomic regions directly targeted by REF6.
source: We next assessed genomic regions directly targeted by REF6 (Cui et al., 2016; Li et al., 2016) and found that the accumulation of H3K27me3 in ref6-5 was associated with a complete loss of H3K27me1 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from ChIP-seq analysis, supported by figure data and citations.

claim: There is a strong reduction of H3K27me1 in clf/swn mutants at REF6 binding sites.
source: We found a strong reduction of H3K27me1 in these mutants at REF6 binding sites (Figure 2C), thus confirming that H3K27me1 at these euchromatic sites is PRC2-dependant.
evidence: This is a finding from ChIP-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: H3K27me1 at euchromatic sites is PRC2-dependent.
source: We found a strong reduction of H3K27me1 in these mutants at REF6 binding sites (Figure 2C), thus confirming that H3K27me1 at these euchromatic sites is PRC2-dependant.
evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq data showing reduction of H3K27me1 in clf/swn mutants.

claim: In ref6-5, the ectopic accumulation of H3K27me3 primarily affected genes that displayed low levels of expression (second to fifth quantiles).
source: We found that while H3K27me3 was primarily associated with strongly repressed genes in wild-type (first three quantiles), in ref6-5, the ectopic accumulation of H3K27me3 primarily affected genes that displayed low levels of expression (second to fifth quantiles) (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from combined ChIP-seq and RNA-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: The activity of REF6 was required for low-level expression genes (third to fifth quantiles).
source: Moreover, we found that the activity of REF6 was required for low-level expression genes (third to fifth quantiles) (Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a finding from combined ChIP-seq and RNA-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: REF6 contributes to gene activation by the removal of PRC2-dependent repressive marks.
source: Collectively, these data support the view that REF6 contributes to gene activation, by the removal of PRC2-dependent repressive marks, and to the maintenance of low-level basal expression, by maintaining H3K27me1 in transcriptionally active chromatin.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data on H3K27me3 and gene expression.

claim: REF6 contributes to the maintenance of low-level basal expression by maintaining H3K27me1 in transcriptionally active chromatin.
source: Collectively, these data support the view that REF6 contributes to gene activation, by the removal of PRC2-dependent repressive marks, and to the maintenance of low-level basal expression, by maintaining H3K27me1 in transcriptionally active chromatin.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data on H3K27me1 and gene expression.

claim: F1 plants from crosses between single and double histone demethylase mutants and wild-type plants were indistinguishable from wild-type.
source: We found that F1 plants from these crosses were indistinguishable from wild-type, however some F2 plants displayed unexpected developmental phenotypes that were not present in either single or double mutants (4.65% paternal and 4.42% maternal transmission, n = 1500 each) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an observation from crossing experiments.

claim: Some F2 plants from crosses between histone demethylase mutants and wild-type displayed unexpected developmental phenotypes that were not present in either single or double mutants (4.65% paternal and 4.42% maternal transmission).
source: We found that F1 plants from these crosses were indistinguishable from wild-type, however some F2 plants displayed unexpected developmental phenotypes that were not present in either single or double mutants (4.65% paternal and 4.42% maternal transmission, n = 1500 each) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an observation from crossing experiments.

claim: The frequency of plants displaying developmental abnormalities in the F2 from F1 hybrids between wild-type and single histone demethylase mutants was markedly lower (0.58% for elf6-C and 0.63% for ref6-5).
source: On the other hand, the frequency of plants displaying developmental abnormalities in the F2, resulting from F1 hybrids between wild-type and single histone demethylase mutants, was markedly lower (0.58% for elf6-C and 0.63% for ref6-5; n > 300 each).
evidence: This is an observation from crossing experiments.

claim: Abnormal plants arising from the elf6-C/+;ref6-5/+ hybrids segregated for the different mutant allele combinations.
source: Intriguingly, abnormal plants arising from the elf6-C/+;ref6-5/+ hybrids segregated for the different mutant allele combinations (Figure 3A), thus indicating that these novel phenotypes are not genetically linked to either elf6-C or ref6-5 mutations.
evidence: This is an observation from genotyping experiments.

claim: Novel phenotypes in F2 plants are not genetically linked to either elf6-C or ref6-5 mutations.
source: Intriguingly, abnormal plants arising from the elf6-C/+;ref6-5/+ hybrids segregated for the different mutant allele combinations (Figure 3A), thus indicating that these novel phenotypes are not genetically linked to either elf6-C or ref6-5 mutations.
evidence: This is inferred from the segregation pattern observed in genotyping experiments.

claim: Two different F5 progenies (A5.B1 and A5.C6) revealed 544 euchromatic loci with elevated levels of H3K27me3.
source: This analysis revealed 544 euchromatic loci with elevated levels of H3K27me3, of which one third were also found to be hyper-methylated in the parental double mutant line used in reciprocal crosses (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from ChIP-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: One third of the 544 euchromatic loci with elevated H3K27me3 in epiERs were also found to be hyper-methylated in the parental double mutant line.
source: This analysis revealed 544 euchromatic loci with elevated levels of H3K27me3, of which one third were also found to be hyper-methylated in the parental double mutant line used in reciprocal crosses (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from ChIP-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: Some of the H3K27me3 imprints present in epimutants were established in elf6-C/ref6-5 and were then stably transmitted over the five generations, even after the wild-type function of these histone demethylases had been restored.
source: These data suggest that some of the H3K27me3 imprints present in epimutants were established in elf6-C/ref6-5 and were then stably transmitted over the five generations, even after the wild-type function of these histone demethylases had been restored (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq data showing persistent H3K27me3 in epiERs.

claim: For both characterized epiER lines, the ectopic accumulation of H3K27me3 was particularly common and strong in constitutive heterochromatin within the pericentromeric regions.
source: Notably, for both characterized lines we found that the ectopic accumulation of H3K27me3 was particularly common and strong in constitutive heterochromatin within the pericentromeric regions (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from ChIP-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: ELF6 and REF6 are necessary to limit the transmission of H3K27me3 imprints to offspring.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that ELF6 and REF6 are necessary to limit the transmission of H3K27me3 imprints to offspring, and that failure to do so results in epigenomic and developmental abnormalities.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data on transgenerational inheritance of H3K27me3.

claim: Failure to limit the transmission of H3K27me3 imprints results in epigenomic and developmental abnormalities.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that ELF6 and REF6 are necessary to limit the transmission of H3K27me3 imprints to offspring, and that failure to do so results in epigenomic and developmental abnormalities.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data on epiER phenotypes and epigenomic changes.

claim: Both epiER lines displayed global reductions in DNA methylation, primarily at pericentromeric regions.
source: We found that both epiER lines displayed global reductions in DNA methylation, primarily at pericentromeric regions (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding from BS-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: There was no ectopic accumulation of H3K27me3 at any genes involved in the DNA methylation pathway, including MET1, DDM1, CMT2 and CMT3, in the parental mutant.
source: This global reduction in methylation occurred despite there being no ectopic accumulation of H3K27me3 at any genes involved in the DNA methylation pathway, including MET1, DDM1, CMT2 and CMT3, in the parental mutant.
evidence: This is a finding from ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: The two analysed epiERs displayed notable differences in DNA methylation levels between lines and among chromosomes.
source: In addition, we found that the two analysed epiERs displayed notable differences in DNA methylation levels between lines and among chromosomes (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding from BS-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: No significant changes in DNA methylation were found in elf6-C, ref6-5 and elf6-C/ref6-5 mutants.
source: Importantly, we did not find any significant changes in DNA methylation in any of these mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from BS-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: While some epiER plants were consistently devoid of DNA methylation at pericentromeric regions, similar to the ddm1 mutant, others displayed intermediate states that varied from chromosome to chromosome.
source: This analysis revealed that while some plants were consistently devoid of DNA methylation at pericentromeric regions, similar to the ddm1 mutant, others displayed intermediate states that varied from chromosome to chromosome, thus providing evidence for a partial resetting of DNA methylation (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from BS-seq analysis on individual plants, supported by figure data.

claim: The loss of DNA methylation in constitutive heterochromatic regions in epiERs was associated with a decrease in methylation at TEs and genes located therein.
source: Notably, the loss of DNA methylation in constitutive heterochromatic regions in epiERs was associated with a decrease in methylation at TEs and genes located therein (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from BS-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: Defects in heterochromatin methylation were also observed in F1 hybrids derived from reciprocal crosses between wild-type and histone demethylase mutants.
source: Moreover, these defects in heterochromatin methylation were also observed in F1 hybrids derived from reciprocal crosses between wild-type and histone demethylase mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from BS-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: In epiERs, heterochromatic TEs that gained H3K27me3 had a proportional loss of DNA methylation whereas euchromatic TEs showed no change in DNA methylation.
source: We found that in epiERs, heterochromatic TEs that gained H3K27me3 had a proportional loss of DNA methylation whereas euchromatic TEs showed no change in DNA methylation (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a finding from combined ChIP-seq and BS-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: A gain in H3K27me3 has a negative effect on the deposition and/or the maintenance of DNA methylation at heterochromatic transposons.
source: These data support the view that a gain in H3K27me3 has a negative effect on the deposition and/or the maintenance of DNA methylation at heterochromatic transposons.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between H3K27me3 gain and DNA methylation loss at heterochromatic TEs.

claim: In epiERs, heterochomatin compaction is strongly affected and manifest as a higher proportion of decondensed nuclei compared to wild type.
source: We found that in epiERs, heterochomatin compaction is strongly affected and manifest as a higher proportion of decondensed nuclei compared to wild type (Figure 4E; Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from immunostaining assays, supported by figure data.

claim: 1240 and 1128 genes were misregulated in epiERs A5.B1 and A5.C6, respectively.
source: To this end, we performed a RNAseq analysis and found that 1240 and 1128 genes were misregulated in epiERs A5.B1 and A5.C6, respectively (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq analysis.

claim: A fraction of the upregulated genes in epiERs (483 and 544) were also upregulated in elf6-C/ref6-5 plants.
source: A fraction of the upregulated in epiERs (483 and 544) were also upregulated in elf6-C/ref6-5 plants (Figure 5A; Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: Most upregulated genes in the epimutants were involved in biotic stress responses.
source: Gene ontology analysis revealed that most upregulated genes in the epimutants were involved in biotic stress responses (Figure 5B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from gene ontology analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: Some deregulated genes in epiERs were located in constitutive pericentromeric heterochromatin and showed the strongest upregulation effect.
source: When we investigated the chromosomal distribution of these deregulated genes, we found that some were located in constitutive pericentromeric heterochromatin and showed the strongest upregulation effect (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: Both RNA and DNA transposon families were significantly upregulated in epiERs.
source: We found that both RNA and DNA transposon families were significantly upregulated in epiERs (Figure 6A; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: One heterochromatic transposon, CACTA1 (At2TE20205), and one euchromatic retrotransposon, EVADE (EVD) (At5TE20395), showed a significant increase in copy number in both epiERs.
source: We found that one heterochromatic transposon, CACTA1 (At2TE20205), and one euchromatic retrotransposon, EVADE (EVD) (At5TE20395), showed a significant increase in copy number in both epiERs (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a finding from copy number analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: CACTA1 and EVADE were depleted in DNA methylation and significantly upregulated.
source: Further analysis revealed that these TEs were depleted in DNA methylation and significantly upregulated (Figure 6C; Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from combined BS-seq and RNA-seq analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: Most novel transposon insertions accumulated in euchromatin, continued to be active over multiple generations, and sometimes disrupted expression of genes that could be linked to the observed developmental phenotypes.
source: Most novel insertions accumulated in euchromatin, continued to be active over multiple generations, and sometimes disrupted expression of genes that could be linked to the observed developmental phenotypes (Figure 6D–F and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a finding from transposon insertion analysis, supported by figure data.

claim: The developmental abnormalities found in epiER lines arise from heritable epigenetic changes and from genetic mutations caused by TE mobilization and reinsertion into the genome.
source: Collectively, our data demonstrate that the developmental abnormalities found in epiER lines arise from heritable epigenetic changes and from genetic mutations caused by TE mobilization and reinsertion into the genome.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data on epigenetic changes and transposon mobilization.

claim: REF6 and ELF6 regulate the removal of H3K27me3 at different genomic loci.
source: Our data show that REF6 and ELF6 regulate the removal of H3K27me3 at different genomic loci; while REF6 has a large repertoire of target genes, ELF6 activity is restricted to a small subset of genes, most of which can also be targeted by REF6.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the ChIP-seq data presented in the study.

claim: REF6 has a large repertoire of target genes, while ELF6 activity is restricted to a small subset of genes, most of which can also be targeted by REF6.
source: Our data show that REF6 and ELF6 regulate the removal of H3K27me3 at different genomic loci; while REF6 has a large repertoire of target genes, ELF6 activity is restricted to a small subset of genes, most of which can also be targeted by REF6.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the ChIP-seq data presented in the study.

claim: Despite the structural similarities between REF6 and ELF6, they are able to carry out distinct functions in H3K27me3 homeostasis.
source: Combined with our genetic analysis, these data collectively suggest that despite the structural similarities between these two proteins, they are able to carry out distinct functions in H3K27me3 homeostasis.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined genetic and ChIP-seq data.

claim: REF6 restricts the spreading of H3K27me3 to the genomic regions flanking PRC2 targets.
source: Our data also support the view that although REF6 restricts the spreading of H3K27me3 to the genomic regions flanking PRC2 targets (Yan et al., 2018), it also has a hitherto unrecognized function in the regulation of H3K27me1 homeostasis in euchromatin.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: REF6 has a hitherto unrecognized function in the regulation of H3K27me1 homeostasis in euchromatin.
source: Our data also support the view that although REF6 restricts the spreading of H3K27me3 to the genomic regions flanking PRC2 targets (Yan et al., 2018), it also has a hitherto unrecognized function in the regulation of H3K27me1 homeostasis in euchromatin.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the ChIP-seq data presented in the study.

claim: The accumulation of H3K27me1 in Arabidopsis relies both on the activity of ATXR5 and ATXR6 in heterochromatin and on the activity of REF6 in transcriptionally active euchromatin.
source: Therefore, the accumulation of H3K27me1 in Arabidopsis relies both on the activity of ATXR5 and ATXR6 in heterochromatin (Jacob et al., 2009; Jacob et al., 2010) and on the activity of REF6 in transcriptionally active euchromatin (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the combined data on H3K27me1 distribution, supported by citations and figure.

claim: ATXR5 and 6 target only newly synthesized H3.1 histone variants, which are deposited during replication and replaced by H3.3 in euchromatin during later stages of the cell cycle.
source: ATXR5 and 6 have been shown to target only newly synthesized H3.1 histone variants, which are deposited during replication and replaced by H3.3 in euchromatin during later stages of the cell cycle (Jacob et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: In mammals, the histone demethylases UTX and JMJD3 catalyze the conversion of H3K27me3 and H3K27me2 into H3K27me1.
source: In mammals, the histone demethylases UTX and JMJD3, also known as KDM6A and KDM6B, have been shown to catalyze the conversion of H3K27me3 and H3K27me2 into H3K27me1 (De Santa et al., 2007; Lan et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2007; Swigut and Wysocka, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Defects in PRC2 methyltransferase activity in mammals completely abolishes the accumulation of H3K27me1 in embryonic stem cells.
source: Moreover, defects in PRC2 methyltransferase activity in mammals completely abolishes the accumulation of H3K27me1 in embryonic stem cells (Ferrari et al., 2014; Montgomery et al., 2005), suggesting a conserved PRC2-mediated mechanism for H3K27me1 homeostasis in euchromatin, in both animals and plants.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: There is a conserved PRC2-mediated mechanism for H3K27me1 homeostasis in euchromatin, in both animals and plants.
source: Moreover, defects in PRC2 methyltransferase activity in mammals completely abolishes the accumulation of H3K27me1 in embryonic stem cells (Ferrari et al., 2014; Montgomery et al., 2005), suggesting a conserved PRC2-mediated mechanism for H3K27me1 homeostasis in euchromatin, in both animals and plants.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of mammalian and plant data.

claim: The deposition of H3K27me1 in euchromatin is dependent on the activity of PRC2 and REF6.
source: The precise mechanism responsible for the deposition of this chromatin mark in Arabidopsis is currently unknown, but our data support the view that the deposition of H3K27me1 in euchromatin is dependent on the activity of PRC2 and REF6 (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the ChIP-seq data presented in the study.

claim: In mammals the presence of H3K27me1 in actively transcribed genomic regions has been associated with the promotion of transcription.
source: In mammals the presence of H3K27me1 in actively transcribed genomic regions has been associated with the promotion of transcription (Ferrari et al., 2014), a fact that may explain why Arabidopsis genes associated with H3K27me1 display moderate levels of expression, whereas the conversion of this mark into H3K27me3 negatively impacts their transcriptional rates.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Arabidopsis genes associated with H3K27me1 display moderate levels of expression, whereas the conversion of this mark into H3K27me3 negatively impacts their transcriptional rates.
source: In mammals the presence of H3K27me1 in actively transcribed genomic regions has been associated with the promotion of transcription (Ferrari et al., 2014), a fact that may explain why Arabidopsis genes associated with H3K27me1 display moderate levels of expression, whereas the conversion of this mark into H3K27me3 negatively impacts their transcriptional rates.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data.

claim: Plant somatic cells accumulate H3K27me3 primarily at protein-coding genes.
source: Plant somatic cells accumulate H3K27me3 primarily at protein-coding genes; however, in reproductive tissues and mutants where DNA methylation is reduced, this mark also accumulates at TEs (Deleris et al., 2012; Weinhofer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In reproductive tissues and mutants where DNA methylation is reduced, H3K27me3 also accumulates at TEs.
source: Plant somatic cells accumulate H3K27me3 primarily at protein-coding genes; however, in reproductive tissues and mutants where DNA methylation is reduced, this mark also accumulates at TEs (Deleris et al., 2012; Weinhofer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: H3K27me3 accumulates at transposon sites in plant species with reduced levels of DNA methylation.
source: Other studies have also reported the accumulation of H3K27me3 at transposon sites in plant species with reduced levels of DNA methylation (Montgomery et al., 2020), as well as in mammal somatic and reproductive tissues which also show reduced levels of DNA methylation (Hanna et al., 2019; Reddington et al., 2014; Saksouk et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: H3K27me3 accumulates in mammal somatic and reproductive tissues which show reduced levels of DNA methylation.
source: Other studies have also reported the accumulation of H3K27me3 at transposon sites in plant species with reduced levels of DNA methylation (Montgomery et al., 2020), as well as in mammal somatic and reproductive tissues which also show reduced levels of DNA methylation (Hanna et al., 2019; Reddington et al., 2014; Saksouk et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The stable inheritance of de novo acquired DNA methylation imprints in plants is well documented.
source: The stable inheritance of de novo acquired DNA methylation imprints in plants is well documented.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Mutations in MET1 and DDM1 frequently induce epimutations caused by DNA hypomethylation.
source: Mutations in the machinery involved in the deposition of DNA methylation, such as the cytosine DNA METHYLTRANSFERASE 1 (MET1) and the chromatin-remodeling DEFICIENT IN DNA METHYLATION 1 (DDM1), frequently induce epimutations caused by DNA hypomethylation (Johannes et al., 2009; Kakutani et al., 1996; Mathieu et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Epimutations caused by DNA hypomethylation in met1 and ddm1 mutants are maintained during sexual reproduction and remain stable over several generations, even after the function of MET1 or DDM1 is restored.
source: These epimutations are maintained during sexual reproduction and remain stable over several generations, even after the function of MET1 or DDM1 is restored.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: Natural epimutations created during asexual propagation and associated with DNA hypomethylation involving TEs can be stable over multiple generations, thus contributing to a variety of novel heritable phenotypes.
source: Moreover, natural epimutations created during asexual propagation and associated with DNA hypomethylation involving TEs, can be stable over multiple generations, thus contributing to a variety of novel heritable phenotypes (Ong-Abdullah et al., 2015; Wibowo et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Analysis of the Arabidopsis met1 mutant has shown that a large number of TEs that lose DNA methylation gain H3K27me3.
source: Additionally, analysis of the Arabidopsis met1 mutant has shown that a large number of TEs that lose DNA methylation gain H3K27me3 (Deleris et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: TEs in Arabidopsis gain H3K27me3 in response to ddm1-induced loss of DNA methylation.
source: Similarly, TEs in Arabidopsis gain H3K27me3 in response to ddm1-induced loss of DNA methylation (Rougée et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: DNA methylation and H3K27me3 act antagonistically to mediate the transcriptional silencing of transposons.
source: Collectively, our data together with these reports suggest that DNA methylation and H3K27me3 act antagonistically to mediate the transcriptional silencing of transposons.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data and previous studies.

claim: There is accumulating evidence for the active role of histone demethylases in resetting H3K27me3 at specific loci during sexual reproduction.
source: There is accumulating evidence for the active role of histone demethylases in resetting H3K27me3 at specific loci during sexual reproduction (Crevillén et al., 2014; Noh et al., 2004) and for a global depletion of H3K27me3 during spermatogenesis (Borg et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: There is a global depletion of H3K27me3 during spermatogenesis.
source: There is accumulating evidence for the active role of histone demethylases in resetting H3K27me3 at specific loci during sexual reproduction (Crevillén et al., 2014; Noh et al., 2004) and for a global depletion of H3K27me3 during spermatogenesis (Borg et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Some of the H3K27me3 imprints that are ectopically deposited in histone demethylase mutants cannot be reset if they are distal to the target sequences recognized by the demethylases.
source: While the precise mechanism(s) governing this phenomenon remains poorly understood, our finding that the failure to reset H3K27me3 during sexual reproduction resulted in its trans-generational inheritance in euchromatin, even when functional demethylase activity was restored, might suggest that some of the H3K27me3 imprints that are ectopically deposited in histone demethylase mutants cannot be reset if they are distal to the target sequences recognized by the demethylases.
evidence: This is speculated based on the transgenerational inheritance data.

claim: Once established, H3K27me3 imprints could be maintained across generations as epimutations through the recruitment of LHP1-PRC2 complexes.
source: Furthermore, once established, these H3K27me3 imprints could be maintained across generations as epimutations through the recruitment of LHP1-PRC2 complexes (Derkacheva et al., 2013).
evidence: This is speculated based on the data and supported by a citation.

claim: The inheritance of H3K27me3 imprints causes defects on the maintenance of DNA methylation at constitutive heterochromatic regions.
source: Our data revealed that the inheritance of H3K27me3 imprints causes defects on the maintenance of DNA methylation at constitutive heterochromatic.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the combined ChIP-seq and BS-seq data.

claim: The defects in DNA methylation maintenance in epiERs are not caused by the ectopic accumulation of H3K27me3 at genes implicated in the DNA methylation machinery.
source: However, these defects are not caused by the ectopic accumulation of H3K27me3 at genes implicated in the DNA methylation machinery.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the ChIP-seq data showing no H3K27me3 accumulation at DNA methylation genes.

claim: The ectopic deposition of H3K27me3 in constitutive heterochromatin may be linked to defects in the resetting of DNA methylation thought to take place during gametogenesis and/or during early embryo development.
source: The ectopic deposition of H3K27me3 in constitutive heterochromatin may instead be linked to defects in the resetting of DNA methylation thought to take place during gametogenesis (Calarco et al., 2012; Ibarra et al., 2012; Slotkin et al., 2009) and/or during early embryo development (Bouyer et al., 2017), where epigenetic modifications have been shown to be anti-correlative (Mathieu et al., 2005; Roudier et al., 2011).
evidence: This is speculated based on the data and supported by citations.

claim: An active resetting of H3K27me3 in gametes would be critical for the re-establishment of DNA methylation.
source: Under this scenario, an active resetting of H3K27me3 in gametes would be critical for the re-establishment of DNA methylation, while the ectopic deposition of H3K27me3 in histone demethylase mutants could antagonize the deposition of DNA methylation at TEs (Figure 7).
evidence: This is speculated based on the model proposed in the study.

claim: The ectopic deposition of H3K27me3 in histone demethylase mutants could antagonize the deposition of DNA methylation at TEs.
source: Under this scenario, an active resetting of H3K27me3 in gametes would be critical for the re-establishment of DNA methylation, while the ectopic deposition of H3K27me3 in histone demethylase mutants could antagonize the deposition of DNA methylation at TEs (Figure 7).
evidence: This is speculated based on the model proposed in the study.

claim: Mutants defective in histone demethylases could accumulate epigenomic alterations in gametes that could explain the heritable, yet unstable, phenotypes observed in epiERs.
source: Mutants defective in histone demethylases could accumulate epigenomic alterations in gametes that could explain the heritable, yet unstable, phenotypes observed in epiERs.
evidence: This is speculated based on the phenotypic and epigenomic data.

claim: Similar epimutations and phenotypic variation have been shown to arise from crosses between wild-type plants and mutants defective in the machinery that maintains DNA methylation.
source: Similar epimutations and phenotypic variation have been shown to arise from crosses between wild-type plants and mutants defective in the machinery that maintains DNA methylation (Kakutani et al., 1996; Kato et al., 2004; Marí-Ordóñez et al., 2013; Mirouze et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: epiERs have defects in the silencing of some transposons resulting in an increase in genetic lesions associated with their mobilization.
source: As in these studies, we also found that epiERs have defects in the silencing of some transposons resulting in an increase in genetic lesions associated with their mobilization.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the transposon analysis data.
